audit: E1 Honshu-Izu coastal empirical ecological-state audit

design.system: Japanese coastal continental and oceanic island plant-pollinator networks

published_state_results.direction_with_distance: reported values decrease with increasing distance for the listed metrics
published_state_results.community_trait_matching_best_model: functional diversity metrics FEve and FD_Q rather than pollinator species diversity
published_state_results.pollination_function_result: lower community-level trait matching is associated with lower community-level plant pollination success
published_state_results.functional_interpretation: low FD_Q partly reflects low abundance of long-tongued pollinators

identification_boundary: Published results support geography-to-functional-state and functional-state-to-function associations, but do not by themselves prove that mainland/island origin or distance has no residual predictive information after conditioning on FD_Q, FEve, trait matching and season.
next_model: Compare held-out prediction of pollination success for E1-M1=functional_state+season versus E1-M2=E1-M1+origin_or_distance, holding out whole sites or site-seasons.
headline: In the Izu system, island geography is an upstream filter, while pollinator functional diversity and flower-pollinator trait matching are the measured conditions most directly linked to pollination function; species richness alone is insufficient.
